thread:
incident-bot: ALERT — SLO breach detected on /generate (tokenizer/preproc path). p95 latency 1.3s, p99 latency 3.2s over the last 5m :warning:

oncall-elena: paging in. getting context... what customer traffic looks impacted?

alex-eng: seeing spikes aligned with requests that have large prompt templates + JSON-mode parsing. profiler shows heavy time in prompt_preproc tokenizer step.
mira-ml: confirmed. sampling traces: 12% of requests (mainly streaming) hit a preproc path that spends ~650ms in template expansion + 400ms in JSON schema validation before tokenization.
sam-sre: where's tail coming from — streaming stalls or model enqueue?
alex-eng: it's pre-tokenizer CPU work blocking worker threads, so streaming stalls while we wait for tokens to be produced. not model-side.
jamie-cs: two customers reported slow responses (AcmeApp, Retailly). AcmeApp support ticket #2342 flagged elevated errors/timeouts.
oncall-elena: impact window? percentage of total requests? SLA risk?
mira-ml: 12% of traffic overall, but for streaming endpoints it's closer to 28% because they use JSON-mode and complex tool schemas. SLAs at risk for customers on enterprise plans hitting p95 > 1s.
sam-sre: let's run through mitigation options. Short term: 1) disable JSON-mode pre-validation 2) route affected routes to dedicated pool with extra CPU 3) enable prefix caching for common templates 4) temporary rate-limit high-template requests.
alex-eng: quick command to disable JSON validation on the routing layer: `redwoodctl flags set preproc.json_validation false --scope route:/generate` — I can run it if oncall approves.
oncall-elena: do it. also start a canary reroute for those customers to dedicated-pool-2: `routectl set-weight --route /generate --pool dedicated-pool-2 --weight 0.2`
ops-bot: ACTION LOGGED: preproc.json_validation disabled by oncall-elena at 2050000045. route weight change queued (0.2).
mira-ml: I'll also push a patch to short-circuit template expansion when template size > 8k tokens (cheap guard). prepping a canary PR.
sam-sre: monitoring set: p95/p99 dashboards updated, alert threshold lowered by 200ms. please post updates.
alex-eng: after disabling JSON validation: p95 dropped to 480ms in 2m, p99 to 900ms. streaming stalls reduced; tail tokens start flowing sooner.
jamie-cs: AcmeApp says latency improved for their test users, but still occasional stalls. they want ETA for full fix.
oncall-elena: next steps: 1) keep validation off for 30m while we test patch 2) deploy template short-circuit to prod canary for 5% traffic 3) if stable, roll to 50% then 100% 4) notify CSMs for impacted customers
mira-ml: deploying canary now. PR includes a defensive fast-path: if template AST has > X nodes, skip deep schema validation and emit a warning token to client.
alex-eng: also enabling prefix/KV caching for these routes: `redwoodctl cache enable --route /generate --type prefix --ttl 10m` — should shave another ~150ms for repeated templates.
ops-bot: METRIC SNAPSHOT at 2050000090: p95=0.48s, p99=0.95s, affected_requests=9%
sam-sre: good. let's keep validation off for at least 1 deploy cycle. tracking: incident severity -> Sev3 for now, can escalate if customer SLA breaches escalate.
jamie-cs: I notified AcmeApp CSM and opened a priority support bridge. Retailly assigned to account owner.
oncall-elena: oncall handoff in 30m to alex-eng. alex, you'll own the post-mortem and customer comms if things look stable?
alex-eng: acknowledged. will collect traces, attach sample payloads, and start drafting timeline.
mira-ml: post-deploy canary shows template short-circuit reduced preproc time from ~650ms to ~80ms on canary traffic. pushing to 50% now.
ops-bot: ROUTE UPDATE: canary -> 5% at 2050000115, then 50% at 2050000130.
jamie-cs: AcmeApp on call bridge confirmed noticeable improvement. asking for an RCA and ETA for full remediation.
oncall-elena: if 50% looks good after 10m, we'll flip validation off permanently and include the short-circuit as the long-term fix. also add telemetry to count skipped-validations.
sam-sre: follow-ups for postmortem: - root cause: expensive JSON-mode validation + large template expansions running synchronously in pre-tokenization thread pool - why wasn't load-shedding engaged? check autoscale triggers for preproc workers - add bounded timeouts to preproc step and fallbacks - surface per-route preproc latency to console
alex-eng: drafting timeline and adding sample traces. will include commands used, metric graphs, and patch links.
jamie-cs: customers updated: AcmeApp happy, Retailly monitoring. CSMs to expect postmortem and mitigation package.
oncall-elena: thanks team. if any regression, re-page. handing to alex for next steps. :white_check_mark:
alex-eng: taking over oncall at 2050000160. starting postmortem doc and will ping when ready.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (monitoring). final snapshot: p95=0.41s, p99=0.88s, affected_requests=2%.
